stem: A bag contains 10 red tokens and some blue tokens. Two tokens are selected at random from the bag, one after the other, without replacement. The probability that both tokens are red is \(\frac{3}{14}\). How many blue tokens are in the bag?
solution: Let \(n\) be the total number of tokens. Then \(\frac{10}{n} \cdot \frac{9}{n - 1} = \frac{3}{14}\).
The positive solution is \(n = 21\), so there are \(21 - 10 = 11\) blue tokens.
verify:
n = symbols('n', positive=True)
sol = solve(Eq(Rational(10) / n * 9 / (n - 1), Rational(3, 14)), n)
assert sol == [21]
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [sol[0] - 10]
